label: copy phase: input s while outputting f (the bigram "s f" being copied), at recall position >= 3
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never in original or delimiter steps). It fires when the fed-back input is s and the current output is f, i.e. the model is copying an original s f bigram. The bigram must sit at least 3 positions into the sequence: with recall_idx 0-1 it is mostly silent, and it is strongest when recall is mid-to-late (lift peaks around recall_idx 4-6). The top activations (up to 2.9) are all s->f transitions, often followed by another f. On the dev split, input s accounts for 96% of activation mass and output f for 90%. Weaker residual activity (about 14% of mass) shows up on f->f (input f, output f, i.e. copying ff), on s->s, and on s followed by other outputs such as z, r, n. These are low-magnitude, mostly in the bottom quartile. It does not fire on first occurrences of a token (in_first=1) or on letters other than s/f as input. Dev: precision 0.92, recall 0.62, mass recall 0.83.

issues: All factual claims check out on the dev profile. Activity is 100% copy phase. There are zero activations at recall_idx 0-1, so 'mostly silent' understates it: it is completely silent. Lift peaks at recall_idx 4-6 (4.2x/4.0x/3.8x). Input s holds 95.7% of mass and input f 4.3%; every other input token gives 0. Output f holds 89.9%. in_first=1 gives 0 activations. Every top activation is s->f.
Test scores reproduce: P 0.926, R 0.621, F1 0.744, mass recall 0.834.
The recall_idx>=3 gate is real. Precision of s->f by recall_idx on test: r1 0.002, r2 0.24, r3 0.87, r4 0.97, r5 0.95, r6 0.94, r7 0.92, r8 0.87. Dropping the gate lowers precision to 0.64 (F1 0.65).

The misses (1097 steps, 16.6% of mass) split into low-precision classes, so they look like weak, scattered spillover rather than a coherent missed class. f->f has precision 0.10 and 4.5% of mass. s->s has precision 0.09 and 4.6%. s->other outputs have precision 0.007. Taking all s inputs at r>=3 gives precision 0.04. Adding f->f to the predicate lowers F1 to 0.62.

One small high-precision subclass is missing: s->s when next_out is f (copying 's s f'), with precision 0.89 but only 1.6% of mass. Adding it raises test F1 only slightly, from 0.744 to 0.756. This is a minor refinement, not a refutation.
The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate. Count recall is lowish (0.62) because of the weak bottom-quartile residue, and the explanation discloses this.
